nodes.text: When a unique current candidate and another candidate each have one explicit version tuple, a larger peer version leaves selection null, all candidates held, and no active-version edge.

Existing current/year conflict checks and valid human decision precedence remain. Changes to selected or unselected candidate contents invalidate the prior human choice and retain stale_human_decision.
Numeric tuple comparison preserves current-newest and current-equal cases, current-absent numeric version ordering, existing year/status cases and candidate-order invariance.
The F04a conflict fixture excludes both competing versions from the real Reader manifest, preserves an unrelated source, validates the generated Reader output and retains source hashes.

All 15 existing synthetic F01 application wiring tests pass on Python 3.14.6 after the resolver change, including publication, binding failure, valid/stale human choice, query and final audit orchestration. Model outputs are fixtures.

The result covers F04a only. Annual/revision identity, candidate completeness, independent version graph validation, HITL generation/revision binding and answer-time freshness remain open. Python 3.9 application and real-model/package acceptance are not claimed.
